speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, could you tell me how long these skin lesions have been present and if they are itchy or painful? Also, have you noticed any other symptoms like fever or joint pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the exposure to chickenpox and the child's up-to-date immunizations, could you describe the appearance of the lesions, specifically if they are flesh-colored, umbilicated, and have a central dimple? I would also like to know if the lesions are increasing in number or spreading to other areas of the body.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation of umbilicated, pearly papules is classic for Molluscum contagiosum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum contagiosum
